## Physical and internal faces (`external`) {#sec-ch03-physfaces}

### Summary

Each named boundary condition becomes a boundary function (bfunc) per face. At construction, on the `slab` and
`cubed` layouts, every face that has a neighbouring block, and every face of a periodic direction, has its bfunc
removed; the exchange then fills its ghosts. The predicate `is_physical_boundary` simply asks whether a bfunc is
installed. On the cubed sphere nothing is removed, so each panel edge keeps the function the card names for it. Cubed-sphere
cards must name `custom`, the no-op, on all four tangential faces; the ghosts are then left to the cubed-sphere
exchange, which does not consult the predicate. A card that names none gets the default `reflecting` on the panel
edges, and nothing refuses it. The boundary conditions themselves are
covered by @sec-ch11.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Decide per block face whether its ghosts come from a boundary function (physical) or a neighbour
(internal): a face is physical exactly when a boundary function is installed on it; a rule, stated in the Derivation
layer.

**Data.** In: YAML `boundary-condition: {external: {x1-inner, ..., x3-outer}}` and the layout's neighbours. Out:
the block's `bfuncs` per face and `is_x1_wall`.

**Placement.** Setup (block construction); read in every sync.

**Activation.** The YAML boundary names; default `reflecting` on every face.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exactly one owner per face; an unknown name stops setup.

**Evidence.** `test_exchange_decomp`, `test_wb_wall_corner`; check `[C18]`; the ctest entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

Local symbols: none; the section is a rule about names and functions.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the scheme is a rule, stated here in full. On the `slab` and `cubed` layouts a face loses
its bfunc when the block has a neighbouring block across it or when its axis is periodic; this is the reset of the
internal `bfuncs` at construction ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}). Afterwards a face is physical exactly when a
bfunc is installed on it, which is all that `is_physical_boundary` tests
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::is_physical_boundary >}}). For a multi-axis offset the first non-zero component in the order $x_3$,
$x_2$, $x_1$ names the face, as `face_of` does in the same lines. On the cubed sphere no bfunc is removed.

The check enumerates the rule as stated: over all 26 non-zero offsets it names exactly one face every
time, splitting them 18 / 6 / 2 between $x_3$, $x_2$ and $x_1$, and on a single-axis offset it returns that
axis's own face; of the four $(\text{neighbour}, \text{periodic})$ combinations exactly one keeps the bfunc, so
"a bfunc is installed" and "no neighbour across it and the axis not periodic" are the same predicate
(`[C18]`).[^pf-c18]

[^pf-c18]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C18]`; a Python enumeration of `face_of` and the bfunc removal in `MeshBlockImpl::reset` at the pin,
    CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The rule runs once, when the block is built. The generic exchange skips every physical face when it packs and unpacks
(@sec-ch03-exchange), so a physical face's ghosts are only ever written by its bfunc. A wall is a narrower notion:
`is_wall_boundary` is true only for the whitelisted names `reflecting` and `fixed_temperature`, which diffusion uses,
and `is_x1_wall` is a physical $x_1$ face that is not periodic, which the gravity work and the wall reconstructions
use. On an axis with one cell no bfunc is installed, so its faces are never physical. @fig-ch03-physfaces-slab shows
a $2\times2$ slab decomposition.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-physfaces-slab
#| fig-cap: "A $2\\times2$ slab decomposition with reflecting $x_2$ walls and periodic $x_3$. Thick black lines are physical faces (a boundary function is installed); dashed reddish-purple lines are internal faces between blocks; dotted lines are periodic faces, which are internal too and wrap around."
#| fig-alt: "Four squares in a two by two arrangement; outer left and right edges thick, inner edges dashed, top and bottom edges dotted."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_physfaces_slab import make_fig
```

: Code map of physical and internal faces. {#tbl-ch03-physfaces-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-physfaces-code):

1. For each live axis the two names are read (default `reflecting`), suffixed `_inner` or `_outer` and looked up;
   an unknown name stops setup with "Boundary function ... is not defined", from the lookup into `bfuncs`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. On `slab` and `cubed`, the constructor removes the `bfuncs` of internal and periodic faces
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}); on `cubed-sphere` it removes none.
3. Every consumer then asks `is_physical_boundary`, `is_wall_boundary` or `is_x1_wall`.

**How to use it.** Name each face; an unnamed face of a live axis gets `reflecting`, and `periodic` on both faces of
$x_2$ or $x_3$ (or of $x_1$ on `cubed`) makes the axis internal:

```yaml
boundary-condition:
  external:
    x1-inner: reflecting
    x1-outer: reflecting
    x2-inner: periodic       # on a cubed sphere: custom on x2 and x3 (all four)
    x2-outer: periodic
```

Refused: an unknown name stops setup with "Boundary function 'reflectng_inner' is not defined.". The default, the
periodic flag and the lookup are ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

```cpp
    auto ix2 = external_bc["x2-inner"].as<std::string>("reflecting");
    if (ix2 == "periodic") op->layout()->periodic_x(true);

    ix2 += "_inner";
    TORCH_CHECK(get_bc_func().find(ix2) != get_bc_func().end(),
                "Boundary function '", ix2, "' is not defined.");

    op->bfuncs().push_back(get_bc_func()[ix2]);
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_exchange_decomp` | internal-face ghosts come from the right neighbour | value bounds | @sec-ch03-layouts |
| `test_wb_wall_corner` | a periodic $x_2$ edge and an $x_2$ split behave as internal faces | $10^{-12}$, exact | @sec-ch03-cornerrefresh |

: Tests that exercise the face classification. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-physfaces-tests}

No test targets the classification alone. The forcing deck records why it must have more than one $x_1$ cell: with
`nx1: 1` no $x_1$ bfunc is installed, `is_physical_boundary` is false at the top and bottom, and every top or bottom
forcing returns early, so a test of them passes on zeros (the header comment of the deck,
{{< code tests/test_forcing_cubed_sphere.yaml >}}). The cases above run on CPU; they were not run for this chapter
at the pin (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- On the cubed sphere the tangential faces carry whatever the card names, `reflecting` by default; only `custom`
  leaves the panel edges to the exchange. `is_physical_boundary` is true at panel edges either way.
- The corner refresh is the one place that answers differently: its own `physical` treats an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face of
  a cubed-sphere block that holds the built-in `custom` no-op as exchange-owned, recognising the no-op by function
  identity with `is_custom_noop`, not by name (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh).
:::

Code that loops over every installed bfunc applies the panel-edge function: harmless for `custom`, but with the
default `reflecting` a six-panel run with tangential flow differs from the `custom` run by about $10^{-3}$ relative
in momentum after 5 cycles (measured on a source build of the pin; at rest the two agree); code that
asks `is_physical_boundary` on $x_2$ or $x_3$ of a cubed sphere would classify a panel edge as physical (inferred from
the code; at the pin the only tangential callers are in the generic layout, which the cubed sphere does not use for
its own exchange; not measured). The corner refresh does not ask `is_physical_boundary`: it reads the installed
functions through its own `physical` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}), so on
a cubed-sphere panel edge holding the built-in no-op the two answers differ. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in
the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
